title: Twisted Gaussian Schell States in Quantum Optics: Twist-Assisted Nonclassicality and Entanglement
summary: We introduce the Twisted Gaussian Schell (TGS) state, a two-mode mixed Gaussian state defined as the quantum-optical analog of the Twisted Gaussian Schell-model beam of classical paraxial optics, characterized by the so-called twist phase. In the TGS state, the twist parameter arises when an asymmetric two-mode thermal state is subject to local squeezing after the action of phase shifters and a beam splitter.
